_comment: The second evaluation round. Run, in this order:
python tools/campaign.py --manifest tools/ewaluacja-campaign.json configs
python tools/campaign.py --manifest tools/ewaluacja-campaign.json references
python tools/campaign.py --manifest tools/ewaluacja-campaign.json sweep        (faza 1)
python tools/campaign.py --manifest tools/ewaluacja-campaign.json budget       (faza 2)
python tools/campaign.py --manifest tools/ewaluacja-campaign.json --only M1 run
Scenes are NOT redeclared here; they are frozen in ewaluacja-manifest.json, which also
carries the phase-0 numbers that justify the set. This file adds only what a campaign
has and a scene list does not: arms, protocols, categories, rounds and repeats.
PROTOCOLS. The first round ran one protocol (30 s, 16 checkpoints). This round runs
four, because the plan asks three different questions of the same pair of arms:
short     equal TIME. One budget for the whole set, chosen in phase 2 so both arms
accumulate a similar number of frames on most scenes. This is the
protocol every basic measurement runs on.
samples   equal SAMPLE COUNT. The budget is a number of path samples, not seconds,
and the arms convert it to different frame counts: the guided technique
draws two path samples per iteration (two-sample MIS at the first vertex)
where path tracing draws one. It answers how well the method steers rays,
with the frame cost taken out - a different question from `short`.
variance  equal VARIANCE. Renders with `checkpoints: every:1`, so every frame is
saved and scored, and the reading is the FIRST frame under an MSE ceiling.
No interpolation. The dense capture inflates this run's own clock (a
measured 6.8-10.4 ms against a 4.63 ms warm-up at 1080p), so the time
column comes from `budget`'s frame cost, never from this run's sidecars.
curve     the 30 s error-against-time curves, the ONLY place 30 s appears. Nothing
in the tables is read off this protocol.
'samplesPerFrame' on an arm is what makes the equal-sample budget expressible: it is
the number of path samples one frame of that arm carries.
'sweeps' is phase 1: one factor at a time, guided arm only, at a common short budget.
The winner per scene lands in parameters.json, which `run` then reads. The grid
dimension is swept over the SCENE's own ladder from ewaluacja-manifest.json, not over
the values listed here, because a rung above a scene's cap measures the cap.
TWO PARAMETERS OF THE PLAN ARE NOT SWEPT, and the chapter has to say why rather than
quietly drop them. Both are compile-time constants and neither is a knob:
* the number of supervoxels is fixed at 32 (Constants::Graphics, kClusterCount).
The cluster-visibility mask is ONE uint32 per superpixel, one bit per cluster, so
64 clusters would need a 64-bit mask and a different kernel - a structural change,
not a setting.
* the number of visibility representatives is fixed at 128 (four 32-bit fingerprint
words). 64 would halve the words and change the fingerprint layout everywhere it
is read.
Both belong in the chapter's table of COMMON parameters, with this reason stated.
CATEGORIES ARE RUN ONE AT A TIME. A job is keyed by (cell, arm), so asking for two
categories whose protocols differ in one invocation is refused by design. Run each
with its own --only and its own --out; M1 and M7 share the protocol and may run
together.

sweeps._note: Not only a quality knob: acceptance of guided samples RISES with resolution (San Miguel 0.1 % at 64^3, 25.4 % at 512^3), so on the large scenes this parameter decides whether the guide works at all. A rung whose lit-voxel census passes 131 072 measures the cap and the sweep refuses it.

0 = binary visibility, 1 = soft average visibility (default), 2 = intensity alone. Mode 2 culls the whole cluster-visibility stage, so it is also the cheapest; the plan's three leaf-value modes are exactly these.
0 = intensity only (default), 1 = the paper's exact geometry + distance term, 2 = the cheap approximation. Not in the plan's list, but it is a real runtime knob and costs the same sweep.

short._comment: Equal TIME at the scale of one display frame, realised by stating the FRAME COUNTS rather than a time budget. A time budget cannot do it here: the engine stops at the first frame reaching the budget, so each arm overshoots by a partial frame and the overshoots differ - measured at 24 ms, the arms landed up to 20 % apart in time, always in the guided arm's favour. The counts in klatki-rownego-czasu.json put both arms within 0-9.3 % of each other around 24 ms (about 40 frames per second). They are derived from frame costs measured IN that regime: cost under a 10 s load runs 2-42 % higher, and the guided arm loses more to the clock-down than the path-traced one. Frame counts differ between the arms by the frame-cost ratio, 2.4-6.1x, and are not asked to agree - that ratio is what is being measured.
short._budget: seconds:0.024 - superseded by framesFrom; kept for the record of what 24 ms meant
short._checkpoints: None on purpose: a 24 ms budget holds 1-37 frames, and eight checkpoints inside it would put up to eight captures into a window that short. Capturing is not free (a measured ~1 ms of machinery plus a resolution-dependent readback per capture), so the frame cost such a run reports would describe the capturing, not the technique. Frame cost comes from the phase-2 runs, which capture once.

samples._comment: Equal sample count. Frames follow from the arm's samplesPerFrame.
samples._samples: 16 path samples: the guided arm draws two per frame, so 8 frames against 16 for path tracing. Chosen to sit at the top of the range the equal-time budget reaches (M1 gives the guided arm 4-16 samples), so the two measurements describe the same regime.

variance._comment: Every frame saved and scored; the reading is the first frame under the MSE ceiling.
variance._budget: per cell, from the 30 s curves: a bit above where each cell crosses the ceiling. A common 512-frame budget would write 15 GB of captures to answer a question most cells answer in the first hundred frames.
variance._mseCeilingWhy: the only ceiling both arms reach on every scene within a few hundred frames; 0.002 needs 1713 frames on veach-ajar and 0.01 is already met at the first checkpoint of the 30 s curve, so it cannot be resolved

short-x2._comment: The equal-time pair multiplied by 2: same ratio between the arms, 2 times the budget. Localises where the guided arm's short-budget advantage ends, which the error curves cannot do below 160 ms because their checkpoints land on wildly different frame counts per arm.

short-x4._comment: The equal-time pair multiplied by 4: same ratio between the arms, 4 times the budget. Localises where the guided arm's short-budget advantage ends, which the error curves cannot do below 160 ms because their checkpoints land on wildly different frame counts per arm.

short-x8._comment: The equal-time pair multiplied by 8: same ratio between the arms, 8 times the budget. Localises where the guided arm's short-budget advantage ends, which the error curves cannot do below 160 ms because their checkpoints land on wildly different frame counts per arm.

curve-short._comment: The 30 s curve's first checkpoint lands at 0.3 s, which leaves the whole real-time regime unmeasured: M1 sits at 19-28 ms and the curve starts an order of magnitude later. On staircase and san-miguel the guided arm leads at 20 ms and trails at 300 ms, so the crossing happens inside that gap. This protocol covers 10 ms to 1 s and joins the two.

curve._comment: The only 30 s protocol; feeds the plot and no table.

SUNTEMPLE._what: komórka diagnostyczna poza zbiorem: jak siatka zachowuje się na scenie o rozpiętości 271 m

M4B._what: krzywe w reżimie czasu rzeczywistego, 1 s - domknięcie dziury między M1 a M4

M1X2._what: drabina budżetu x2 na dwóch scenach z przecięciem

M1X4._what: drabina budżetu x4 na dwóch scenach z przecięciem

M1X8._what: drabina budżetu x8 na dwóch scenach z przecięciem

M7C._what: wariant z ponownym użyciem próbki na krzywej 30 s - obciążenie ujawnia się powyżej przecięcia
M7C._deviation: The plan asks for a SHORTER second budget for this measurement, arguing that the bias shows above the crossing of the two curves. Those two statements contradict each other: above the crossing means LONGER. The base budget is already one display frame, so a shorter one would be a single frame. Measured here on the 30 s curve instead, which brackets the crossing from both sides.
